A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Bandit Multiclass List Classification. Their complete main texts, algorithms, equations, and Appendices A–B support comparison, including matching the relocated online regret analysis.

before.justification: V1 reports algorithms, theoretical bounds, and proofs, but no original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis results.

after.justification: V2 remains entirely theoretical, including its new appendices. Its empirical optimization objective is analyzed mathematically rather than evaluated in reported experiments.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 replaces stochastic Frank–Wolfe with SPIDER gradient estimates and successive sample batches with ordinary Frank–Wolfe on a fixed empirical objective. V2 also adds a specialized single-label algorithm that collects correctly guessed examples before optimization. The online algorithm is retained in Appendix B.

E1.justification: Neither version actually trains or evaluates on datasets or benchmarks. The added single-label specialization is a theoretical treatment, not additional empirical task coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated empirical comparators. Comparisons with EXP4 and prior single-label work concern theoretical guarantees.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental evaluation protocols. Revised sample counts and iteration budgets are prescriptions for theoretical algorithms, not settings of conducted experiments.

E4.justification: Neither version contains ablations, sensitivity tests, robustness evaluations, or empirical case studies. The additional appendix analyses are mathematical proofs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Concentration inequalities and variance bounds form part of the theoretical analysis.

E6.justification: Neither PDF contains measured performance results or empirical result entries. Changes to sample-complexity and oracle-complexity guarantees are theoretical changes assessed under T1.

T1.justification: V2 replaces the stochastic optimization analysis with new uniform-convergence and Rademacher-complexity lemmas and a deterministic Frank–Wolfe analysis. Theorem 1 changes the additive polynomial term from (K/m)^10 to K^9/m^8; Appendix A.3 adds the K^7 single-label bound and proof. V2 also corrects the negative-log objective and minimization-oracle signs, and requires an ERM oracle accepting only nonnegative reward vectors.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution summary add a distinct claim of improving the cited single-label PAC bound from a K^9 additive term to K^7. V1 primarily claims generalization of that earlier work. The leading PAC-rate, sparsity-adaptation, and online-regret claims remain.

C2.justification: Appendix A.3 explains the single-label improvement through collecting fully labeled examples and using Lipschitz-based uniform convergence. The discussion revises the explanation for the remaining high dependence on K, shifting emphasis from stochastic Frank–Wolfe smoothness to accurate objective minimization for gradient control. The full-bandit and infinite-class open problems remain.

D1.justification: Parameter documentation changes from SPIDER batch schedules and step sizes 1/t to fixed-sample optimization with step sizes 2/(t+2), explicit point-mass initialization, and direct ERM weight construction. Appendix A.3 specifies sample and iteration counts for the new specialization. Neither version supplies code or hardware information.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Foster and Rakhlin, Frank and Wolfe, Jaggi, and Shalev-Shwartz and Ben-David, while removing the Yurtsever et al. SPIDER reference. It positions the single-label result as improving Erez et al. (2024a), while retaining most of the existing related-work discussion.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the exposition around PAC learning: the online section moves into Appendix B, Appendix A gains a new subsection structure, and the central optimization explanation and contribution summary are rewritten. The discussion becomes Conclusion and Open Problems with an added concluding overview.

P2.justification: Algorithm 1's display is expanded, the stochastic Frank–Wolfe panel is replaced, a single-label algorithm panel is added, and the online algorithm panel moves to Appendix B. The basic single-column layout and algorithm-display style remain; neither version contains empirical result plots or tables.

improvement.justification: V2 corrects the PAC objective/oracle sign inconsistencies and presents a simpler, more explicit optimization procedure with supporting analysis and a new K^7 single-label guarantee. These improve clarity and strengthen a useful special case. The gains are qualified by the general additive bound, K^9/m^8, which can exceed v1's (K/m)^10, and conflicting Frank–Wolfe iteration bounds in Section 3.1 and Appendix A.2.
